Menu values and tool scores are fitted predictions. Use the observed evidence, state a testable short hypothesis, and specify edits that match displayed candidate identities on the pinned GFP reference. All eligible candidates are from a fixed menu. Do not estimate or cite measurements for candidates. Keep all text fields concise and evidence-specific.

arguments.analyst: Recent single-mutant observations show high brightness for V193A and P187T, while A227V and A179S are also bright; acidic E213K is low. Prioritize menu candidates with conservative substitutions and avoid interpreting predictions as measurements.
arguments.hypothesis: Among these menu designs, candidates composed of conservative substitutions will more often retain high fluorescence than disruptive substitutions; this can be tested by comparing their measured brightness.

decision.analyst: Recent single-mutant observations show high brightness for V193A and P187T, while A227V and A179S are also bright; acidic E213K is low. Prioritize menu candidates with conservative substitutions and avoid interpreting predictions as measurements.
decision.hypothesis: Among these menu designs, candidates composed of conservative substitutions will more often retain high fluorescence than disruptive substitutions; this can be tested by comparing their measured brightness.
decision.critic: Tool estimates are fitted predictions, not measurements; the observed examples are too few and varied to establish a reliable conservative-edit effect.
decision.selection_rationale: Prioritize C22, whose estimate is highest among the evaluated candidates, followed by C21 and C19. C32 and C37 complete the set with estimates near the lower end. This is a test of the tentative idea that conservative substitutions retain fluorescence; the weakness is that the observations do not directly test these edits or predict their combination effects.
